frames.narration: A backend service wants to tell user 42 about a new comment. It does not know where user 42 is. It sends 'to user 42: comment 9' to the fan-out router.
The router asks the registry where user 42 is connected. The user has two devices on two nodes: the phone on gateway 17 and the laptop on gateway 04.

messages.label: c-91 on gw17, c-92 on gw04

frames.narration: The router gives the message the next sequence number for this user, 119, stores it in the resume buffer, and publishes one message to each node's topic. Every node sees only its own topic.

Each gateway receives the message from its topic and finds the local socket for connection c-91 or c-92. The writes are asynchronous, and the gateway first checks that the connection's queue is not full.
The laptop receives the comment straight away. The phone has entered a tunnel and the network is gone, so its socket is silent. Gateway 17 does not know yet.

Gateway 17 sends its 30-second ping and gets no pong after two intervals, so it closes the connection and removes the registry entry. A message that arrives now would find only the laptop, and also be kept in the buffer.

The phone leaves the tunnel and reconnects after a random delay of a few seconds, not at a fixed moment, so that thousands of phones in the same tunnel do not return together. The load balancer sends it to gateway 17 this time, and it says: my last sequence number was 118.

The gateway fetches everything after 118 from the resume buffer and replays it: message 119 arrives, in order. The phone applies it once. The registry gets the new entry, and the phone is up to date with no full refresh.
